_comment: Swiss Ephemeris data files fetched by ci/fetch_swiss_ephemeris.py. These are
the four files this service needs to run on real ephemeris data instead of
swisseph's built-in Moshier fallback.
THREE consumers, all going through this one manifest and this one fetcher:
* the `ephemeris` build stage in Dockerfile — the SHIPPED image bakes these
files in, so a deployment carries its own data and a rollback to an image
digest is a rollback to that image's data;
* the same stage in Dockerfile.test, so the local Docker loop needs nothing
downloaded by hand;
* the swiss-ephemeris CI job (CALC-1), which runs the suite against them.
This comment used to say a CI run exercised 'the data the image is
volume-mounted with in production'. That was never true. No volume mount was
codified in any environment, the deployment's Cloud Run module has no volume
support at all, and no build ever fetched these files into the image. Measured
2026-07-31 inside the image digest a deployed revision was actually serving:
data/ephe held 0 files, no *.se1 existed anywhere on the filesystem, and
probe_ephemeris_source() returned retflag 65604 with FLG_MOSEPH set. Baking the
files into the image is what makes that sentence true rather than aspirational.
The files are distributed under the Swiss Ephemeris dual licence (AGPL-3.0 or a
paid Professional Licence); this service uses them under AGPL-3.0 — the same
licence it ships under — so fetching them, and shipping them inside an image
that is itself AGPL-3.0, is within those terms. They are deliberately NOT
committed (see .gitignore: data/ephe/): ~2 MB of binary data with its own
licence does not belong in this git history, and fetching at build time keeps
the checksum pin load-bearing on every build.
SOURCE: the upstream Swiss Ephemeris distribution repository (aloistr/swisseph),
pinned to a COMMIT sha rather than a branch, so the path itself is
content-addressed and cannot move under us. EPHEMERIS_LICENSE.md used to point at
https://www.astro.com/ftp/ephe/, which is dead; the paths actually probed are
recorded structurally in 'known_dead_sources' below rather than in this prose,
so ci/tests/test_ephemeris_license_doc.py can fail if that doc ever presents one
of them as a live instruction again. This manifest is the source of truth for
where the data comes from, and that doc must agree with it.
sha256 is trust-on-first-use, exactly like a lockfile entry: recorded from the
first verified download and pinned thereafter, so a later silent change to a
published file fails the job instead of quietly shifting every golden value.
Updating one is a reviewable diff, never an automatic refresh. A null sha256 is
NOT 'skip the check' — the fetcher fails closed and prints the value to record.
Ephemeris-DATA directory paths EPHEMERIS_LICENSE.md used to send readers to.
Each measured 404 on probed_date. Recorded as data, not prose, so a guard can
read it: ci/tests/test_ephemeris_license_doc.py fails if any of these appears
in that document outside its 'Dead links' section.
SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY: these three paths were probed. That is NOT a finding
about astro.com as a whole, and the doc must not generalise it into one -- it
used to say 'every astro.com variant of it' while, two paragraphs earlier,
still sending readers to an astro.com URL for the Professional Licence. A
claim wider than its measurement is how a doc starts contradicting itself.
